consent.standardReminder: Cloud checks send the exact claims you approve to Google Gemini with Google Search. Details
consent.standardBannerBody:
Standard mode. Toulmin checks claims on this device when it can. You choose which claims to send to Google Gemini in the cloud (a paid service, through Firebase); you see the exact text first. Each claim is sent with the evidence Toulmin found for it: abstracts, openly licensed full text, and — only if you allow it — text from PDFs you added. Cloud checks use Google Search: Google keeps those prompts and search results for 30 days to provide grounded answers, and does not use them to train its models. Reference titles and DOIs are sent to Toulmin's servers and to OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and Crossref to look up your references. The built-in sample manuscript can be checked in the cloud with one click, because it contains no text of yours.
To protect the service from abuse, Toulmin uses Google reCAPTCHA Enterprise, which sends signals about your browser and device to Google.
consent.confidentialNotice: Confidential mode. Confidential keeps your manuscript text on this device: claim checking runs only here. Reference titles and DOIs are still looked up — they are sent to Toulmin's servers and to OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and Crossref — unless you turn on DOI-only lookup (references without a DOI then can't be checked). To protect the service from abuse, Toulmin uses Google reCAPTCHA Enterprise, which sends signals about your browser and device to Google.

devpost.testingInstructions:
1. Open https://toulmin.web.app/ in Chrome on a desktop computer and click 'Try a sample manuscript'. Every feature works without signing in. The sample is editable: type a new claim and watch it being checked. Imported multi-file projects (.zip, .docx) open as read-only audit copies.
2. In Standard mode, click 'Check the sample in the cloud' to send the sample's five predefined claims to the cloud check in one click. Public cloud checks are a cost-bounded daily preview: this sample check is shared by all visitors for up to 20 runs a day. With a judge code, the sample check and every other cloud check use the reserved judge quota instead.
3. To see whether each check ran on this device or in the cloud, open Proof mode from the ⋯ menu in the header (⋯ → Proof mode). It turns on automatically after you enter a judge code.
4. To use the reserved judge quota, open the ⋯ menu, choose 'Judge access' and enter one of these codes. Each code works on up to 5 browsers or devices: {CODE_1}, {CODE_2}, {CODE_3}, {CODE_4}, {CODE_5}, {CODE_6}, {CODE_7}, {CODE_8}, {CODE_9}, {CODE_10}. If a code does not work, contact us through the Devpost judging contact and we will send a replacement.
5. On-device checking needs Chrome 148 or later on a computer with 22 GB of free disk space and either a graphics card with more than 4 GB of memory or 16 GB of RAM and 4 CPU cores. On other computers Toulmin explains why the on-device model is unavailable: choose Confidential for reference checks only, or Standard and 'Use cloud fallback for this document' to see the cloud fallback.
6. Android: install the APK from {APK_URL} (allow installs from this source, then open Toulmin). This APK is an offline demonstration of the Pocket Ledger on the bundled sample manuscript: it runs Firebase AI Logic on-device inference on the phone, including checks against a printed table or a typed lab note you photograph (printable pages: {PRINT_PAGES_URL}). It needs a phone with Gemini Nano through AICore.
